messages:
alex: Heads up — EU2 provisioning is noisy after last night's BMC firmware push. ~34 nodes rolled with the boot-policy flag flipped (secure boot ON). About ~14% of GPU capacity in eu2 is stuck in 'provisioning' or PXE-failed.
chandra: on it, can you drop the firmware version + job id?
alex: FW: bmc-fw-2.14.0-rc3, job: prow/infra/fw-rollout/2026-03-22-03. Canary looked OK but auto-advance kicked.
maria: Was the canary specifically gated on console/PXE? or only heartbeats?
alex: Only heartbeat + basic health checks. Looks like VLAN/eth0 mapping flaked under this fw; some nodes come up with SecureBoot=ON and PXE disabled.
infra-bot: Canary roll advanced -> prow/infra/fw-rollout/2026-03-22-03 :: batch 2/12
sre-oncall: Seeing provisioning queue spike for eu2-gpu-1 pool. Autoscaler can't attach NVMe on some hosts; estimated capacity loss ~60 GPUs. Opening incident.
chandra: Plan: 1) pause rollout (done) 2) mark affected hosts HOLD 3) rollback fw on affected 34 nodes 4) reprovision smoke canary 5) resume with explicit boot-policy gating. Kicking rollback for 10 nodes now.
alex: Paste of recent BMC logs from one repro host:
```
[IPMI] 03:04:12 Error: SecureBoot=ON, PXE disabled
provd: pxe: failed to handshake (0x09)
kernel: nvme0: timeout waiting for attach
```
maria: Can we temporarily route non-critical training and batch jobs to us-east1? Cost impact ~+10% for cross-region but buys time for rollback without hurting SLAs.
ops-lead: Non-prod already shifted. For prod/dedicated customers we'll need to throttle new enqueues in eu2 rather than move prod jobs cross-region — risk/contract obligations.
alex: Noted. I'll notify customer-ops for any dedicated-pool impacts (affected: dedicated-eu2-g1 cluster).
deploy-bot: Rollback job started: ci/infra/bmc-rollback/1782345702 on 10 nodes
sre-oncall: Incident INC-5482 created and pinned runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/bmc-bootpolicy-drifts — add any postmortem notes there.
maria: Quick mitigation ask: can the serving runtime avoid kernels that probe NVMe early? A short-term kernel-selector override might reduce boot-time failures for ongoing reprovision attempts.
chandra: Good idea but that's medium-term. For now I'm running manual rollback + explicit check: `provctl smoke --tests pxe,vlan,console` after each host comes back.
infra-bot: Provisioning queue eu2 peaked at 312 (baseline ~20). Autoscaler paused by manual hold.
ops-lead: After rollback, let's run a bounded canary (5 hosts) with the boot-policy flag explicitly asserted/ignored per runbook. Need engineering signoff before full resume.
alex: Agreed. After the 10-node rollback completes we'll run the 5-host gated canary and only resume if smoke green. Updating the rollout job with a hard stop on boot-policy diffs.
chandra: I'll follow up with a short blameless note and an action item: add a boot-policy gate to the rollout pipeline and a preflight vlan mapping test.
maria: Thanks. any ETA on the first rollback batch completing?
chandra: ~15–20m for first 10 nodes, then run smoke, report back.
alex: Thanks team. Please ping here when rollback done or if we need to escalate to CAD/exec for capacity moves. :thumbsup:
